claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs lines 29-38: `var order = await repository.FindAsync(orderId) ?? throw new KeyNotFoundException($"order {orderId} not found");` then `order.Status = "cancelled"; await repository.SaveChangesAsync(); notifier.Send(order.Id, "order cancelled"); return order;`. No read of order.Status anywhere in the method. Code block in section 5 matches the source character-for-character.

OrderServiceTests.cs@stage-1 has exactly two cancel tests (lines 46, 58): NewOrder seeds Status="new" and asserts "cancelled"; UnknownOrder asserts KeyNotFoundException for id 999. Neither reads FakeNotifier.Sent; no test seeds "shipped". Lines 65-67 comment: "No test here cancels a `shipped` order. The suite is green". `dotnet test DonHang.Tests` at stage-1: Passed 5, Failed 0. git grep -i cancel in DonHang.Tests finds no other file.

story-example.md@stage-1 line 5: "hủy đơn hàng chưa thanh toán của mình"; AC3 (l.14-15): "Khi đơn ở trạng thái `paid`, `shipped` hoặc `cancelled`, nút \"Hủy đơn\" không hiện."; AC4 (l.16-17): "trả về 403 và không thay đổi gì"; AC5 (l.18-19): "lần thứ hai trả về 409"; DoD l.24: "Có test tự động cho mọi tiêu chí chấp nhận ở trên."

OrderServiceTests.cs@stage-1 contains 5 tests: three PlaceOrderAsync, CancelOrderAsync_NewOrder_SetsStatusCancelled, CancelOrderAsync_UnknownOrder_Throws. None seeds paid/shipped/cancelled, none involves another customer (403) or a second cancel (409).

Review practice stated by the outline itself (track.yaml outline items 1-3, near-verbatim); no versioned official doc governs it and the lesson hedges item 3 ("may be passing"). Treated as the lesson's method, not a factual claim.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, and overstated: a test seeded with a cancelled order and asserting "cancelled" does not pass "whatever the service does" — it fails if the service throws, returns a different Order, or sets another status. It only passes when the service leaves the status untouched (the bug the quiz q4 scenario describes). Same absolute wording in quiz q4 explanation.correct (en and vi: "nó qua dù service làm gì").
issues.fix: Replace with: "passes even if the service never changes the status." In quiz q4 explanation.correct use "so it passed even though the service never changed the status" / vi "nên nó qua dù service không hề đổi trạng thái". Add the sentence to claims (kind behavior, section 4).

issues.text: Comparative ranking ("cheaper") not established in the body; section 4 only says such tests are "worth asking about before the merge, not after a bug report". Summary line 5 introduces a cost comparison with no support.
issues.quote: Asking for a missing test before the merge is cheaper than finding the gap after a bug report.
issues.fix: Replace line 5 with: "A missing test is worth asking for before the merge, not after a bug report: without it, nothing fails when that behavior breaks."

issues.text: "without anyone noticing" is absolute; people (QA, users, reviewers) can notice. What the lesson can support is that no test fails.
issues.quote: A missing test means the next change can break that behavior without anyone noticing.
issues.fix: Change to: "A missing test means the next change can break that behavior and the build stays green." Apply the same wording to misconception 2 and quiz q2 explanation.b if kept consistent.

issues.text: Unlisted code fact: "`OrderServiceTests` uses fresh fakes in every test". True at stage-1 (every test does `new FakeOrderRepository()` / `new FakeNotifier()`), but it is a claim about the repository and is not in the ledger. Rated minor because it is verified and restates a prerequisite.
